domains.name: Tickets & Transcripts
domains.promise: Members open support from an owner-branded panel by button or dropdown into a private ticket thread visible only to them, staff manager roles, and the bot; staff claim tickets atomically, manage participants, and close with a saved HTML transcript delivered to the transcript channel and optionally the creator; commerce refund and store support requests route through this same ticket system; inactive tickets are warned and then auto-closed.

controls.description: How members pick a ticket type on the panel message: one button per type or a single dropdown select.
List of ticket type bindings, each with an id, label, button color, emoji, and optional per-type category, manager-role, intro, and intake-form overrides.

constraints.shape: array of { id, label, color, emoji, description, category-override, manager-role-override, intro-message-override, intake-form }

controls.description: Maximum simultaneously open or claimed tickets one member may hold on a panel before further opens are refused.
Role ids granted access to every ticket on the panel with claim, participant, and lifecycle powers.
Category under which open ticket spaces are created; empty string means the panel channel's own category.
Category closed tickets are parked under; empty string leaves closed tickets in place.
Owner-authored intro posted in every new ticket; empty string uses the branded built-in welcome.
Panel-level modal fields shown before the ticket is created, each with label, placeholder, style, required flag, and length bounds; empty list skips the modal.

constraints.shape: array of { label, placeholder, style, required, min-length, max-length }

controls.description: Staff channel where the HTML transcript file is posted on close; empty string disables the channel post while the database copy is still saved.
Whether the closing transcript is also sent to the ticket creator as a DM attachment.
Hours of silence in an open ticket before a warning embed is posted.
Hours of silence before an open ticket is auto-closed; must exceed the warning threshold.
Whether a one-to-five star feedback prompt is posted for the creator when a ticket closes.

defaults.rationale: One labeled, colored button per ticket type is the most discoverable entry point for members.
A general support type plus a dedicated store-and-billing type out of the box, so commerce refund and purchase help routes through the same ticket system from day one.
One open ticket per member keeps queues honest and prevents accidental duplicates; owners can raise it.
No staff roles until the owner assigns them; until then ticket access is creator plus bot only.
Tickets stay near the panel until the owner organizes them into a category.
Closed tickets stay in place until the owner designates an archive category.
The branded built-in welcome greets the member until the owner writes their own.
Zero-friction opening by default; owners add intake questions when triage needs them.
Transcripts are always saved to the database; the staff channel post activates once the owner picks a channel.
Members get their own copy of the conversation by default — member-respectful record keeping.
A full day of silence earns a gentle nudge before anything closes.
Two silent days auto-closes the ticket, keeping staff queues clean without surprising members.
Star-rating feedback on close gives owners a support quality signal by default.

permissions.action: Open a ticket from the panel button or dropdown, completing the intake modal when configured
permissions.enforcement: The panel interaction handler creates the ticket for the clicking member, subject to the max-open-per-user cap, and grants view access only to the creator, the configured manager roles, and the bot.

permissions.actor: Guild member holding no configured manager role who is not the ticket creator
permissions.action: Claim, reopen, or delete a ticket, or run /ticket add and /ticket remove to change participants
permissions.enforcement: Lifecycle button and /ticket subcommand handlers re-check manager-role membership (creators may close their own ticket), reply with an ephemeral branded denial, and write an audit row for the denied attempt.

permissions.actor: Dashboard user with owner or admin access to the guild
permissions.action: Create, edit, repost, or remove ticket panels and read stored transcripts on the dashboard tickets pages
permissions.enforcement: Dashboard session auth plus Supabase RLS restrict ticket_panels and ticket_transcripts access to authorized guild administrators.

messages.trigger: A member opens a ticket from the panel
messages.surface: Intro embed posted in the newly created private ticket thread with Close, Claim, and Transcript buttons
messages.audience: The ticket creator and staff holding a manager role
messages.defaultTemplate: Welcome {member-name}! This is ticket {ticket-number} — {ticket-type-label}. A staff member will be with you shortly. For store or billing questions, include your order number so we can help faster.

messages.trigger: A member at the max-open-per-user cap tries to open another ticket
messages.surface: Ephemeral reply to the panel interaction
messages.defaultTemplate: You already have {open-count} open ticket(s), {member-name} — let's wrap those up before starting another.

messages.trigger: A ticket is closed via the Close button, /ticket close, or the inactivity auto-close
messages.surface: Close embed in the ticket thread carrying Reopen and Delete buttons
messages.defaultTemplate: Ticket {ticket-number} was closed by {closer-name}. This thread is now locked and a transcript has been saved. Thanks for reaching out!

messages.trigger: A transcript is generated on close or via /ticket transcript
messages.surface: Transcript channel post with the HTML file attached and, when enabled, a DM to the creator
messages.audience: Staff in the transcript channel and the ticket creator
messages.defaultTemplate: Transcript for ticket {ticket-number} — {message-count} messages, saved for your records.

messages.trigger: An open ticket passes the inactivity warning threshold
messages.surface: Warning embed in the ticket thread
messages.defaultTemplate: This ticket has been quiet for {idle-hours} hours. It will close automatically if nothing more is needed.

messages.trigger: Ticket creation fails after a panel interaction
messages.surface: Ephemeral reply to the member plus an owner alert channel post
messages.audience: The invoking member and the guild owner
messages.defaultTemplate: I couldn't open a ticket for {member-name}: {failure-reason}. Nothing was created and it's safe to try again.
I couldn't save the transcript for ticket {ticket-number}: {failure-reason}. The ticket itself is intact — run /ticket transcript to retry.

values.description: The panel message is posted with per-type buttons or a dropdown and listens for open interactions.
A private ticket thread exists, visible only to the creator, configured manager roles, and the bot, with a sequential ticket number and an open tickets row.
A staff member holds the ticket via the atomic claim; the claim is recorded on the tickets row.
Close was requested; the transcript is being generated and stored before the status flips.
The ticket is locked: the creator cannot send, Reopen and Delete controls plus the feedback prompt are posted, and the thread is parked in the closed category when configured.
The ticket is marked deleted and its thread removed; the stored transcript and the anonymizable audit trail remain.

transitions.trigger: A member clicks a type button or picks a dropdown type, completing the intake modal when configured
transitions.expectedEffect: Exactly one private ticket thread and one open tickets row are created with the next sequential ticket number, and the branded intro with Close, Claim, and Transcript buttons is posted.

transitions.trigger: A manager clicks the Claim button
transitions.expectedEffect: The status flips from open to claimed atomically; a concurrent second claimer is told the ticket is already claimed and nothing double-applies.

transitions.trigger: Close button, /ticket close, or the inactivity auto-close threshold
transitions.expectedEffect: Transcript generation starts before the status flips so the saved record captures the full conversation.

transitions.trigger: Close button or /ticket close on a claimed ticket
transitions.expectedEffect: Same closing pipeline as an unclaimed ticket, with the claimer recorded on the row.

transitions.trigger: Transcript stored and close bookkeeping finished
transitions.expectedEffect: The tickets row is closed with closer and reason, the creator's send permission is revoked, the close embed and feedback prompt post, the thread moves to the closed category when configured, and the transcript is posted to the transcript channel and DM'd per configuration.

transitions.trigger: A manager clicks the Reopen button
transitions.expectedEffect: Status returns to open, the creator's send permission is restored, the thread moves back to the open category, and a reopen embed posts.

transitions.trigger: A manager clicks the Delete button
transitions.expectedEffect: The tickets row is marked deleted with a timestamp and the thread is removed while the stored transcript survives.

transitions.trigger: The owner edits and saves the panel on the dashboard tickets page
transitions.expectedEffect: The existing panel message is edited in place when possible, otherwise reposted once, and the stored message id is updated — never two live panels.

failures.trigger: Discord rejects creating the private ticket thread because of missing permissions or limits
failures.expectedBehavior: No tickets row is written, the member receives the branded failure reply, the owner is alerted with the concrete reason, and a fresh attempt after the owner fixes permissions succeeds cleanly.

failures.trigger: The tickets insert fails after the private thread was already created
failures.expectedBehavior: The just-created thread is deleted as compensation so no orphan space remains, the member is told nothing was created and may retry, and thread and row never diverge.

failures.trigger: Transcript generation or the ticket_transcripts insert fails during close
failures.expectedBehavior: The close itself still completes so the member is never trapped in a half-closed ticket, the owner is alerted with a retry hint, and /ticket transcript regenerates and stores exactly one transcript afterward.

domains.name: Message Logging
domains.promise: Only after the owner deliberately enables it and picks a staff log channel, member message edits and deletes are captured as branded forensic embeds — before-and-after content, preserved attachments, author, channel, and jump link — under strictly per-guild configuration and per-guild caches; bot messages, embed-only updates, and the log channel itself are never logged; every member holds the full data-rights trio over their own stored records — a self-service readable view and a portable JSON export via the member-facing surface plus /forgetme deletion — each scoped strictly to their own data in their own guild, and member erasure requests anonymize retained forensic data rather than silently keeping it.

controls.description: Master switch for forensic message logging; while off, no edit or delete is captured anywhere.
Staff channel that receives edit and delete embeds; empty string means no valid destination and logging cannot activate.
Whether content edits are captured as before-and-after embeds when logging is on.
Whether deletions are captured with preserved content and attachment links when logging is on.
Channels excluded from capture for privacy; the log channel itself is always excluded regardless of this list.
Lifetime of the per-guild message-log configuration cache; dashboard changes take effect within this window without a restart.

Whether members may self-service the view-and-export half of their data rights — reading their own stored message-log records and downloading a portable JSON copy via the member-facing surface; the /forgetme delete half stays available regardless of this switch.

defaults.rationale: Privacy-aware forensic logging is opt-in: nothing is captured until the owner deliberately turns it on and chooses where it goes.
No destination until the owner picks a staff channel; enabling requires an explicit channel choice.
